subject: Clarify pass-through carveouts & liability allocation for CloudMarket reseller addendum
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cloudmarket.co>; legal@cloudmarket.co
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify pass-through carveouts & liability allocation for CloudMarket reseller addendum

Sara / CloudMarket legal team —

Thanks again for taking the time on this partnership. As we work through the reseller addendum (MSA + Order Form mapping), a couple of areas came up in our review that we want to resolve before we push the redline to procurement:

1) Pass-through fee carveout scope — CloudMarket's current draft appears to permit pass-through of any third-party fees (payments processing, marketplace commissions, cloud provider surcharges). We need to limit the carveout to fees that are: (a) invoiced directly to the end customer via CloudMarket's platform and (b) itemized on the Order Form or invoice traceable to the transaction.

2) Liability allocation for reseller transactions — Redwood is comfortable with pass-through of amounts charged to customers, but we cannot accept unconstrained reseller indemnities or broad liability for partner platform outages. We propose reseller liability be limited to direct damages related to Redwood-authored product defects, with a cap tied to the affected Order Form value (suggested: 12 months of recurring fees).

3) Evidence / audit requests — CloudMarket asked for open-ended audit rights in section 8; we can accommodate on-demand evidence for malware/abuse and invoice trail requests, but we request standardization: (a) SOC 2 report access or equivalent (redacted), (b) invoice/export showing fee flow for disputed transactions, and (c) a 30-day window to respond to requests. No live production access.

Attached are: (i) our marked redline PDF with inline snippets we recommend, and (ii) a mapping spreadsheet that ties pass-through categories to invoice line items.

Can you review and flag any items you consider non-starters? If possible, we'd like to get alignment this week so operations can finish the billing mapping. If something needs legal escalation, please point to the specific clause so we can surface to our VP of Partnerships.

Thanks —

Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0192

Attachments: CloudMarket_Marketplace_Addendum_20270622_redline.pdf (redline), pass-through_fee_mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet mapping)

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cloudmarket.co>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@cloudmarket.co; tom.alvarez@cloudmarket.co
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify pass-through carveouts & liability allocation for CloudMarket reseller addendum

Mina —

Appreciate the clear note and the redline. I pulled a couple of the items into the team for triage. A few quick responses:

• Carveout scope: we understand restricting to platform-invoiced fees, but CloudMarket needs the ability to pass through any fees we actually incur from upstream providers for a given transaction. We can accept your "itemized on the Order Form" requirement, but our concern is operational: if a third-party surcharge is applied after initial procurement (billing adjustment), we need a documented process to surface it.

• Liability: our standard position is to avoid putting an explicit cap on reseller liability for acts of gross negligence or willful misconduct; for ordinary breaches we are open to a capped remedy. Can you confirm Redwood's proposed cap mechanics (12 months of recurring fees) and whether that is per-Order-Form or aggregate per-customer?

• Evidence/audit: we agreed with limiting scope, but legal would like to preserve the ability to request supporting documentation in connection with disputes and regulatory inquiries. We are unlikely to provide live production access; SOC 2 and invoice exports are reasonable. We would propose a 45-day response time though.

Would you be available for a short call tomorrow (Wed) at 10:30 PT to walk the redline? If not, we can take another pass with inline comments.

Best,

Sara Kim
Sr. Counsel, Partnerships | CloudMarket
legal@cloudmarket.co

> On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 09:12 AM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Sara / CloudMarket legal team —
> > (original message quoted)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: suggested positions for pass-through & liability (notes for call)

Team —

Quick internal summary and suggested language before we jump on CloudMarket's call. I reviewed the attached redline and have three recommended positions to present:

1) Narrow pass-through carveout (acceptable compromise):
- Proposed snippet: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Reseller may pass through third-party fees only where such fees are (i) invoiced to the End Customer via Reseller's platform and (ii) explicitly identified as a separate line item on the Order Form or invoice tied to the applicable transaction. Reseller shall provide Redwood, upon reasonable request, an invoice export or transaction report sufficient to reconcile amounts charged to End Customers."

2) Liability cap mechanics (make it Order-Form scoped):
- We should accept 12 months of recurring fees as the cap, but clarify that the cap applies per affected Order Form and is not an unlimited aggregate across customers. Exclude gross negligence and willful misconduct from the cap.

3) Evidence/audit (firm boundaries):
- Accept SOC 2 (redacted) and invoice exports, deny any clause implying live production or unfettered access. Add a 30-day response turnaround and a requirement that requests be accompanied by a reasonable description of the disputed transactions and (where applicable) an executive summary prepared by CloudMarket within 10 business days.

Next steps: Mina, confirm if you want Ben to present the legal snippets on the call or if you'd prefer to hold them offline and circulate to CloudMarket first. If CloudMarket resists the Order-Form scoped cap, escalate to VP Partnerships (we should be prepared to trade a modest concession elsewhere — e.g., more permissive invoice timing — but not uncapped pass-through).

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Commercial | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

> On Tue, Jun 22, 2027 at 10:05 AM Sara Kim <sara.kim@cloudmarket.co> wrote:
> > Mina —
> > Appreciate the clear note and the redline...

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@cloudmarket.co>, legal@cloudmarket.co
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify pass-through carveouts & liability allocation for CloudMarket reseller addendum

Sara —

Thanks — that time works for us. I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 10:30 PT (30 minutes) and attach the redline and our suggested snippet in the invite so we can walk it live.

To confirm prior points so the call can be efficient:
• Redwood will present a carved definition limited to platform-invoiced, Order-Form itemized fees.
• Liability cap: we will propose 12 months of recurring fees, applied per Order Form, excluding gross negligence and willful misconduct.
• Evidence: we accept SOC 2 redacted and invoice exports; Redwood requests a 30-day response window (we will discuss whether CloudMarket can accept 30 vs 45 days).

If CloudMarket signals that the cap/Order-Form scope is a showstopper, we will escalate to our VP Partnerships; please flag in advance if you need an exec on your side.

See you tomorrow —

Mina
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachments (also on invite): CloudMarket_Marketplace_Addendum_20270622_redline.pdf, pass-through_fee_mapping.xlsx
